7150 niktá 'washed, purified' RV. [√ nij ] Wg. nĩtə - 'bald', Dm. nitói ; — replaced in MIA. by
* nikka -: Pk. ṇikka - 'clear'; Woṭ. nik 'thin'; K. nyukᵘ ,
f. nicᷴ 'fine, small' (whence nikun 'to become small'),
ḍoḍ. nikko 'small'; L. P. nikkā 'small, young', awāṇ. nik 'shortness', khet. nikṛā 'small', nikī aṅgəl 'third
finger'; WPah.bhad. nikṛo 'small', bhal. nikki lo f.
'early dawn', nikṛo 'younger', cur. nikkā 'small'; Ku. niko 'good, kind', gng. nik ; N. niko 'healthy, well'; A. nikā 'clean'; B. nikā 'to wipe, plaster with cowdung';
Or. nika 'fine and clean (only of rice)', nikā 'sweeping a
house clean', nikāibā 'to cleanse'; Mth. nĭ̄k 'good', nikāh , Aw.lakh. nīk ; H. nīkā 'good, beautiful' ( nekā infl. by Pers. nēk ); OMarw. nīkā adv. 'well'; G. nīkũ 'clear, pure, fine'; M. nikā 'pure, good'. — See * nigna -. * anikta-; *niktāṅga -. Addenda: niktá-: A. nikāiba 'to cleanse' AFD 337.
